slides.title: Tactile Curiosity Drives Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: The TacEx framework uses tactile feedback to guide curiosity-driven exploration, enabling robots to discover complex contact dynamics and improve manipulation skills. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction through enhanced sensory-driven exploration.

card.one_liner: TacEx uses tactile-weighted epistemic uncertainty to drive robots toward contact-rich interactions for efficient manipulation learning.
card.key_idea: Decomposes model uncertainty across sensory modalities and applies a weighting vector to prioritize the tactile channel, anchoring curiosity to physical touch rather than uniform state-space noise.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in simulation via reward-free exploration (pick-and-place) and post-training frozen VLAs on LIBERO-90 tasks; results show increased interaction frequency and higher success rates.
card.limitation: Not validated on physical hardware; does not enforce safe contact forces; uses fixed hyperparameters for modality weights.

slides.title: OccluDex: Hierarchical 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Learning for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation under Self-Occlusion
slides.highlight: OccluDex integrates global 3D geometry with local tactile contact information to maintain state estimation during self-occlusion, supporting the ego-exo and physics-based skill estimation goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: OccluDex enables robust egocentric dexterous manipulation under severe self-occlusion using hierarchical 3D visuo-tactile representations.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical 3D encoder uses multi-scale masked autoencoding to fuse global point-cloud geometry with local tactile contact tokens via cross-modal attention.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Faucet Rotation and Tabletop Reorientation tasks; outperformed VTDexManip and VTT-3D in simulation and achieved zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: The current framework uses sparse, binarized tactile sensing and lacks support for high-density or lateral fingertip contact information.

slides.title: What to Attend, What to Keep: Skill-Conditioned Visuotactile Representation with Progress-Guided Event Memory
slides.highlight: This work proposes a skill-conditioned representation that dynamically fuses vision and touch using a sparse event memory to retain terminal observations. It significantly reduces delays in slip detection and twist completion for contact-rich robotic tasks.

card.one_liner: SkillFormer uses skill-conditioned fusion and sparse event memory to improve visuotactile representation for contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: A Transformer that conditions fusion of modality-specific short-term windows on a language-described skill, while attending to a sparse memory of terminal observations from previous skills.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on lamp replacement, bottle capping, and blind search tasks using MSE, Pearson correlation, and detection delay; outperformed vision-only and SOTA progress models.
card.limitation: Performance degrades when critical inputs, such as tactile data for contact-rich skills or event memory for search tasks, are removed.

slides.title: PneuTac: Tactile Manipulation with Soft Pneumatic Robots via Unified MPM-Gaussian Splatting Simulation
slides.tldr: UNIFIED SIMULATION FOR TACTILE-GUIDED SOFT ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: PneuTac integrates the material point method and 3D Gaussian splatting to simulate soft pneumatic robots and tactile sensors, enabling the training of policies that outperform baselines in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: PneuTac is a unified simulator for soft pneumatic robots with tactile sensors using MPM and Gaussian Splatting.
card.key_idea: Couples Material Point Method (MPM) for dynamics with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for rendering, utilizing surrogate networks for fast action and perception simulation.
card.evaluation: Tested on a custom soft finger and three-chamber arm across three contact-rich tasks; outperformed baselines using sim-augmented demonstrations.

slides.title: Learning from Runtime Feedback through Failure-Bank Self-Evolution for Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: FailBank converts runtime feedback into persistent policy improvements for vision-language-action models, supporting the MIMIC goal of modeling agent-environment interactions in complex societies.

card.one_liner: FailBank converts runtime safety feedback into persistent policy improvements for Vision-Language-Action models via self-evolution.
card.key_idea: A four-stage framework using an observe-only CBF teacher to collect counterfactual corrections and successful anchors, updating the policy through guarded LoRA adapters.
card.evaluation: Tested on VLA-Arena static-obstacle suite using $\pi_0$ and $\pi_{0.5}$ backbones. Results show improved success rates and reduced policy-induced cumulative cost.
card.limitation: Currently limited to continuous flow-matching policies and static obstacles; dynamic scenes would require temporal obstacle prediction.

slides.title: DiFF: Doppler-informed Flow Matching for Human Motion Flow
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE FRAMEWORK FOR HUMAN MOTION FLOW ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces DiFF, which uses Doppler-informed motion priors and a KAN-based model to improve human motion flow estimation from 4D radar, enhancing a foundational representation for human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: DiFF uses Doppler-informed flow matching and KANs to estimate high-fidelity human motion flow from 4D radar.
card.key_idea: A generative framework combining a Doppler-informed motion prior for initialization with a KAN-attention feature extractor and conditional flow matching to regress non-rigid human motion velocity fields.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on milliFlow and mmBody datasets against SOTA baselines; achieved millimeter-scale 3D endpoint error (2.1mm on mmBody) with high inference efficiency.
card.limitation: Currently uses linear flow paths and is not yet extended to multi-person scenarios or occlusion handling.

slides.title: Multi-Link Safety Filtering for VLA Policies Around Moving Hazards
slides.tldr: TRAINING-FREE SAFETY SHIELD FOR VLA POLICIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-free shield that uses ellipsoids and sparse optical flow to protect multiple arm links from moving hazards during VLA policy execution.

card.one_liner: A training-free safety shield protects VLA policies from moving hazards using multi-link ellipsoidal barriers.
card.key_idea: Combines a CBF-QP barrier program guarding five arm ellipsoids with sparse optical flow to track hazard movement without repeated neural network detection.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SafeLIBERO and a new moving-hazard benchmark; reduced collisions from 65.62% to 27.27% and increased safe-success to 50.43%.
card.limitation: Lacks continuous-time invariance guarantees due to discrete-time updates, RGB-D estimation errors, and potential infeasibility of the barrier program.

slides.title: IronMind: Scaling Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation via Camera-Space Ego-Centric Pretraining
slides.tldr: SCALING HUMANOID DEXTERITY VIA EGOCENTRIC PRETRAINING
slides.highlight: IronMind uses a camera-space action representation to bridge the embodiment gap between human egocentric video and humanoid robots. This approach is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction by enabling scalable pretraining for dexterous manipulation.

card.one_liner: IronMind scales humanoid dexterous manipulation using a camera-space action representation pretrained on 10,000+ hours of egocentric video.
card.key_idea: A VLA model using a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with flow-matching action experts, bypassing body-retargeting via camera-space representations and optional multimodal world-prior supervision during pretraining.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via open-loop metrics, policy-in-the-loop rollouts, and real-robot tests on IRON-R01; 10,000-hour model achieved 55.0% success on six OOD tasks.
